name: DNA polymerase preparation
summary: Kornberg's group partly purified an E. coli enzyme that builds DNA from its building blocks, making DNA synthesis in a test tube possible.
description: Lehman, Bessman, Simms and Kornberg prepared substrates, partially purified an E. coli DNA polymerase and assayed DNA incorporation.
tier_reason: A reusable DNA-synthesis reagent capability supports sequencing and later synthesis/amplification methods, not just the original physical preparation.

date.label: by 1957
date.basis: Detailed purification/assay work was submitted 10 October 1957 and published in 1958; this is a by-date, not a first-discovery claim.

events.statement: Lehman, Bessman, Simms and Kornberg prepared substrates, partially purified an E. coli DNA polymerase and assayed DNA incorporation.
events.caveats: Partial purification is not a pure modern reagent. The authors’ rationale came from coenzyme chemistry; no double-helix-to-enzyme invention edge is claimed.

evidence.supports: Preparation, assay, place and pre-publication date.

date.basis: Date of the cited public report or documented event.

events.statement: Lehman and colleagues described the preparation and assay in the Journal of Biological Chemistry.
events.caveats: No particular other laboratory’s use of the same partially purified preparation is established here. Earlier 1956 work reported partially purified E. coli fractions S and P with different assay framing; equivalence to this detailed 1958 preparation has not been established.

evidence.locator: J. Biol. Chem. 233, pp. 163–170, title, methods and issue date
evidence.supports: Published preparation and assay offered a route for biochemical researchers to learn the procedure.
